notes.title: Selenetrope Devlog 2
notes.content:
[h1]Devlog 2[/h1]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Where I've been[/h2]
I promise I'm still working lol.  I took a month off this January to focus on a side project for a bit to work through some of the burnout.  However, before I took that break I made some massive strides towards finishing the game.  I'd say as it is now we're very nearly feature complete for the initial release.

[h2]What's done so far?[/h2]
[b][u]If you're not interested in reading this whole post at least read this[/u]: Selenetrope is now a more traditional survival horror game with combat and resource management.  I kept the jumpscares from the demo.[/b]  I've also completely changed the setting and aesthetic, which may be unwelcome for some of my wishlisters, but nonetheless I think it had to be done.  [b]The game is now a sci-fi horror mystery taking place in a colony deep beneath the surface of a moon in interstellar space.[/b]

[h3]Mechanics[/h3]
[list]
[*]I've created a central power system which is used to turn on the lights and various interactable objects like electronic doors.  I am still considering modifying it a little bit to make it a bit more interesting, but for now I consider it done.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208662/96348217c0e9607f763ef5a9d2b4ee2f5ab254d9.gif[/img]
[*]There is now a new inventory with a new UI.  You can take, drop, craft, and use items here.  There are a limited number of spots, but you'll increase your maximum as the game goes on.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208662/77255c673772d823fdc315819f53ff5244082248.gif[/img]
[*]I've added weapons and ammo.
[*]Enemies can now be killed with weapons.  Unfortunately they don't tend to stay dead for long...
[*]Enemy spawning and chases have been changed a bit.  They no longer spawn on a timer, but spawn when you make enough noise next to holes in the floor and ceiling.  
[*]I've fully finished the fever and seizure status systems.  When your temperature reaches a 106 degrees you will begin to have a seizure.  If you do not take fever reducers before the seizure is done, you have a chance of acquiring a permanent affliction.  Afflictions are essentially passive debuffs that last until you respawn or find a cure.  I've only created about 4 afflictions as of now, but I'm planning on having about 15 before the game launches.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208662/0dfd0fe99748e339e8e6250d24962bfb36ed44e8.gif[/img]
[*]I've added in robots that wander around doing various tasks.  Their behavior is extremely simplistic.  There are three kinds right now; a standard service bot, a garbage collection bot, and a security bot.  The security bots are really the only ones with a significant impact on gameplay.  Service bots wander and sometimes speak to the player.  Trash bots function as small containers that occasionally contain consumable and craftable items.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208662/83f732c9d657eec54ca4217ea684ef4ee44487bc.gif[/img]
[*]Security systems have been added as well.  If you trigger an alarm you cause a lockdown, which disables automatic electronic doors in your area until the alarm has shut off.  Triggering the alarm also alerts nearby monsters and security bots.  Right now security bots don't trigger any alarm when they see you, but I might eventually change that.  Security bots currently just follow and shoot you when you linger too long in their line of sight.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208662/cf6d241d6ce62200ff34ed5782f63fde67dcd3f7.gif[/img]
[*]The death and revive systems different as well.  You now have a revive in addition to a standard save and load system.  Revives are a finite resource however, so you have to use them carefully.  It also comes at the cost of having to go back and retrieve your resources from where you last died.  I'm considering adding more gameplay modifiers that result from repeated revives, but likely I won't be sure what to add until the game is in the pre-release polish phase.
[*]There is also the new air filtration system to manage while playing.  If it breaks down you have to go and repair it, or risk suffocating on toxic fumes.  There is also a respirator item that allows you to breathe when the filter isn't working, but you cannot hold it to your face and hold a gun at the same time.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208662/5f147c191f2ccdff89622cb9fc0a452c0963828e.gif[/img]

That's pretty much the sum of it.

[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]What's left to make?[/h2]
Mostly content.  This week I'm going to remove a bunch of the old assets from the game and begin modeling new ones.  Unfortunately that is going to take a while.  I've changed the release date one last time to Q2 2025.  I intend to release before or in June regardless of whether or not I'm completely satisfied with the result.  I've been building levels as a pastime for the duration of the redesign, and I've gotten much much better.  Unfortunately I don't have anything good enough to ship in the full game, but I plan to change that this week as well.

There is also a bunch of writing that I need to at least get started on for the in-game lore and notes you find around the colony, but I'm not too worried about that.  It's mostly flavor text and diegetic tutorials and hints.

I'm aiming for about an hour of content for the early access release.  Being generous, there's probably about 10 minutes of content currently, but that lack is because I've been mainly focusing on the features that support the content.  I want to release the most polished product I can, so I'm allowing myself an extra month or two of work time to put together more interesting levels and a better story, and hopefully a more visually appealing game overall.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Thank you[/h2]
Alright, thanks so much to every one of you who made it this far through the devlog.  I really appreciate it.  I'm going to edit the store page and trailer some time soon, but I need to buy a new pc before I can fully do that.  My current setup is painfully underpowered for Unreal Engine, with 2gb of vram and 8gb of ram.  Somehow I've been able to manage so far with such a low powered computer, but I've gotten tired of it.  I hate how often Unreal crashes because I'm out of RAM or VRAM, and I cant' stand not being able to run the game comfortably on anything besides the lowest possible settings.  So, hopefully that makes development easier at least lol.  

If you have any questions about the game going forward, feel free to reply to the event below!

notes.title: Boo
notes.content:
[h1]We are so back.[/h1]
Happy Halloween!  I've been working hard on the game since I posted last Wednesday and I'm in the mood to share some of what I've been working on.

However, before we get started...
[h2]Sorta important announcements[/h2]
[b]I'm going to be taking the demo down on Monday, so if you haven't played it and you really really wanna, I suggest you go do that.[/b]  Keep your expectations low and you might even like it!  Think of it as a little taste of what the game's not gonna be like.
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Something or other[/h2]
Here's what I've finished in the past week since I was last here, and also some stuff that's been decided for certain that was kind of up in the air last week.
[h3]Mechanics[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fully functioning graphic inventory system.  It's done and it works yay.  It's super ugly right now because I'm using placeholder assets, but you probably get the idea.  
[*]The inventory space is also now limited, with expansion upgrades available as a collectible.  (There's actually no upgrade item right now, but I set it up to be pretty plug and play so it'll be there whenever I remember to add it in)
[*]Equippable weapons and items framework is complete.  It's less jank than the old one, but still needs some polish.  I still have to make a bunch of animations.
[*]Crafting is for certain and for real, absolutely definitely in the game for real this time.  It's classic Resident Evil style combining though, so don't expect anything ultra complicated.  All that's left for that is making it feel less wonky in the UI.  Honestly the hardest thing for me to do lately has been making the UI interfaces not feel like doodoo.
[*]The sum total of craftable items right now: a health recovery item, a low durability single use weapon, and a throwable weapon.  I need to make sure the rest of my mechanics and game loop are solid before I go ham with this, so there's not much I can do for certain without potentially wasting time.
[*]Status effects galore!  You can now get hurt and bleed, have seizures, and the base fever mechanic is already functioning well.  Getting dangerously high fever temperatures is what causes seizures.  There are various other debuffs and statuses I'm currently working on, but for these I'm not yet sure what's definitely gonna be included.  I really wanted to make it so you could throw up, but I've honestly got no idea how to do a nice player camera animation without some sort of root motion solution.  I guess I could just let it be ugly...
[*]New pause screen with settings and inventory as tabs in the layout.  Just improved usability.
[*]New interface design for popups.  The result of this right now is I now have combination locks that I'll place on doors in the game.
[*]Notes tab in the pause screen that will hold objectives and little written story snippets found on pieces of paper throughout the environment.  Will also include keycodes (for combination locks).
[*]I've made various physics improvements in general.
[*]One last small thing that ended up being a major improvement in feel; you no longer have to click twice when opening pause and inventory screens, and you no longer have to click to regain camera control after unpausing.  Feels so much better.
[/list]
[h3]Monsters[/h3]
[list]
[*]Some monsters that were previously broken by the code changes have been added back in.  The faceless was already working last time I posted, but I want to tweak his behavior heavily.  I've got a few ideas for him in particular...  
[*]The headless baby (rotisserie chicken) is also in the game and does bleed damage when it launches itself at you.  I genuinely like it a lot.  
[*]Crows are back!  You can now also shoot the crows out of the air.  They also give you bleed, but because of their speed they do less damage.  I found when playing that they're a lot more fun to fight in small clusters as opposed to the huge 300 bird swarm from the trailer.  Also due to the nature of the old map I couldn't let them use traditional navigation, but now I think it's viable, although I'll have to see.
[*]The playdough lookin enemy from the trailer (the one mad doggin u thru the window) is also back in.  He works beautifully too, better than I expected.  He's wasn't in the demo, but all he does is kill you if you look at him for too long enderman style.  Occasionally he'll teleport behind you or to other inconvenient locations.  In order to make him more dangerous I was thinking of making it so he approaches you slowly while you're not looking and attacks, so you have to balance the risk of instant death if you look too long and slow damage if you expose your back.  
[*]The large naked man from the demo is getting a rework too, sometime soon.  I think I'm going to make him more dangerous, but less present.  I've got a nice idea, but it's heavily dependent on the level design so I'm waiting to implement it.  Also he will now be afraid of fire so you can scare him off with that.  Before release I'm gonna tweak or make a new jumpscare for him because I realize his is pretty underwhelming.
[*]And lastly the one with the pretty smile.  I'm currently reworking her behavior right now, but because her MO is to play tricks on you, I need to wait until I've got more gameplay designed before I can decide the best tricks.
[*]Currently I have no plans to add any new monsters leading up to the early access release.  Post launch I'm definitely considering it.  We'll have to see how good the originals are by themselves.  I have a bunch of silly ideas that I could throw in relatively quickly, but that kind of thing doesn't add a whole lot of value.
[/list]

[h2]uh oh[/h2]
And that's pretty much it.  I was going to get a bunch of screenshots to post here, but I decided I'd wait until the game is a little more presentable (especially the UI it's ucky).  I'm going to put together a test level for myself to see how all of my mechanics work together in tandem later this weekend, so I'm hoping I can use that to show off the new gameplay stuff all at once.  I was gonna finish with a long paragraph about some cool new mechanics that weren't quite finished yet, but I decided that was probably not a fantastic idea.  I'll let them speak for themselves next month lol.  All right thanks for reading this far and for caring about my game, or if you don't care, your patience.

One last thing to note about my work on the game since I started the redesign; I haven't made any destructive edits yet.  And by that I mean that everything for the original Selenetrope version still works.  So in the event that someone wants to play the old version just for laughs or whatever, it's not impossible. Eventually I'm going to have to get rid of a lot of that content in the main project, but I have backed up all the edits since the demo release so it's not a big deal.

byeːsteamboredː

notes.title: [IMPORTANT] Selenetrope Major Redesign Devlog
notes.content:
[h1]Devlog 1[/h1]

Now that next fest is over I'm going to share what I've been working on since I released the demo two weeks ago.  After seeing and hearing player responses to the demo I've decided to shift gears a bit and rethink some fundamental aspects of the game.  I realized that as it is now, the game needs some serious changes to become something actually fun and playable.  Some major mechanics and content will be going away in favor of new ones.

As a quick summary, I'm changing the visual style of the game, removing the sleep and hunger systems, removing physics "puzzles", removing the first area from the demo, adding combat, and I'm redesigning the gameplay loop as a whole.

[h2]When Will We See These Changes?[/h2]
I wanted to address this nearer the top so that more people would see it and so no one gets the wrong idea.  These changes will not be passed on to the demo, the demo is staying as is.  These changes will likely only be seen once the early access build has been published.

[h3]How Will This Affect the Release Date?[/h3]
Not sure yet.  I think it's likely I'll have to push back the release.  I'll make sure to make a post once I know for certain whether or not I can make the end of November.  If I'm proud of what I got by the end of next month I might just release a shorter version of the game than originally intended just to get it in the hands of players.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]What's Going Away?[/h2]

[h3]Mechanics[/h3]
[list]
[*]Hunger is being removed.
[*]Sleeping as a means of saving is being removed as well.
[*]Building is going away for now.  I'm undecided as of yet on whether or not this is a permanent decision, but it will not be included in the first early access version of the game.
[*]Advanced movement like wallrunning is no longer going to be a core mechanic of the game.  Although I'd like to come back to it in the future.
[*]All crafting is being removed temporarily.
[*]Physics based "puzzles" like those in the demo are going away as well.  Stuff like hallways being blocked and you need to push the right thing or drag up a table from somewhere else.  The trouble with physics is its unpredictability, and I personally witnessed basically every player I watched struggle with some physics quirk at some time or another.  Another problem is conveyance; for example in the demo there are objects that can't be moved arbitrarily despite looking identical to other moveable objects.  This was a necessity for the game at some points and other times it was just an accident, but either way this can lead to frustrating scenarios where someone tries to push past a shelf that can't be moved.  Or even worse, they could encounter an immovable shelf and just ignore all shelves thereafter under the logical assumption that that kind doesn't move.  So in short, these specific kinds of puzzles are being removed because of their inconsistent rules, and a lack of overall player control.
[/list]
[h3]Levels[/h3]
[list]
[*]The escape section is being removed.
[*]Right now I'm looking into the possibility of removing all loading doors in favor of level streaming, but how that'll actually turn out remains unclear.
[*]The whole level you see in the demo is being taken out of the base game.  
[*]The levels will no longer change shape based on how many times you've slept.
[/list]
[h3]Game Loop[/h3]
[list]
[*]The night system will not function as it did previously.  You will no longer progress to the next night by sleeping.
[*]Both altars are being removed, as the night system no longer exists either.
[*]I'm removing the huge doors that open on a timer as a consequence of the night system changing.  The doors will still exist, but they'll operate differently.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]What's Changing?[/h2]
[h3]Visuals[/h3]
[list]
[*]I've decided for now to go for a more stylized look for the project going forward.  I spent who knows how many hours just tweaking graphics settings in order to make my game performant and good looking, and haven't managed to really succeed at either one.  As a result of that I've decided to move in another direction.  The art style is kind of in flux right now, but I've gotten some interesting results experimenting with it, so we'll see.  More updates on that in the future.
[/list]
[h3]Mechanics[/h3]
[list]
[*]The old player character and code has been completely thrown away in favor of a clean slate.  This means movement has changed significantly.
[*]The physics interactions from the demo have been changed to something more tactile for the player.  So no more headbutting shelves to arrange furniture and stuff.  Instead you can now press a button to pick up and move light objects and the same button to push or pull heavy objects.
[*]Doors are now physics objects.  Specific ramifications for gameplay are still unclear for now.
[*]The inventory system is changing to a limited one with distinct slots.
[/list]
[h3]Level Design[/h3]
[list]
[*]The scale of the levels is going to shrink dramatically.  For the time being I'm going for one mid-sized to large level with distinct small sections.  The idea is to have less space, but to do more with that space in terms of gameplay.
[*]The game is going to remain fundamentally nonlinear, however I'm now emphasizing chokepoints of linearity that all players are funneled into in order to have more control over the player experience.
[*]Goodbye endless samey hallways.  I personally liked the idea of making a huge sprawling labyrinth of tunnels, but actually making it was becoming boring and difficult.  Not only that, but it was hard for players to navigate, and became tiresome relatively quick.  So instead I'm working on making levels with visually distinct rooms and sections.
[/list]
[h3]GameDesign[/h3]
[list]
[*]My focus on gameplay design is shifting towards a more replayable and arcade-like aspect with stricter failure states and emergent gameplay, as opposed to the deliberately crafted spaces from before.  Attempting to put together specific moments of gameplay for the player over the past month made me realize I was stretching the mechanics of my game really thin over wide areas.  Inevitably that meant the vast majority of the time wasn't spent doing anything interesting, and the player wasn't really forced to make any intentional decisions or tradeoffs.  Anyways it's difficult to get into gameplay specifics right now as it's all in the design phase, but it's definitely beginning to take shape.
[*]Exploration and discovery is still going to be a crucial aspect of the game, but it'll be more focused than before.  There are a few new mechanics that demand exploration as a means of survival that definitely incentivize risk in more meaningful and interesting ways than the old sleep, time, and hunger systems.
[*]For now the emphasis is changing from exploring vast spaces into attaining mastery over smaller spaces that get more familiar (and yet more dangerous) over time.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]What's New?[/h2]
This is the more tentative part of the devlog as everything here is in active development so it's likely to receive changes, but what's written below is the stuff most likely to make it into the early access build.  I'll keep everything up to date in future devlogs.

[h3]Mechanics[/h3]
[list]
[*]Combat is getting a bit more emphasis in the new versions of the game, both as a deterrent and as a means to actually kill monsters.
[*]Sickness system...  so the hunger and sleep systems are gone for now, and this is what we have instead in their place.  It's very simple; you take medicine to reduce your fever, if your fever gets too high you get weak, noisy, and slow.  The consequences for extremely high temperatures haven't fully been decided yet, I've got a few ideas though.
[*]Resource management is now going to be a fundamental problem you have to solve while playing the game.  You'll need to decide whether you should carry ammunition, medicine, or tools...
[*]Proper hiding places are on the list of things to get through for the next version.
[/list]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]End[/h2]
All right! Thanks so much for reading, and I'll be back here sometime next month with a new update.  For now I'm changing the release date on the steam page from November to Coming Soon, just in case lol.  Anyways, I sometimes post updates and screenshots on my twitter so feel free to follow me there as well if you'd like to keep up with my daily work.  
Link to my [url=https://x.com/Spinmousing]Twitter/X[/url] right here!
